swett-legitimacy.speaker: Laura Swett, FERC Chairman
swett-legitimacy.evidence: PJM is facing a grave legitimacy crisis. Some transmission owners are openly discussing leaving the RTO altogether. Put plainly, market participants have lost confidence in PJM's decision-making abilities.

lacerte-quagmire.speaker: David LaCerte, FERC Commissioner
lacerte-quagmire.evidence: This is a cultural quagmire that they've developed by eroding the board in the past and creating this fear of [board members] being terminated to where they're not using their authorities. They're not engaging with the states because they don't want to get out of line with what the stakeholders want.

mills-committed.speaker: David Mills, PJM President and CEO
mills-committed.evidence: We are fully committed to rise to the challenge.

ferc-september.speaker: Utility Dive report of the Commission's stated next steps
ferc-september.evidence: FERC will hold a dispute resolution forum in September with PJM stakeholders to develop a governance reform package. If no agreement is reached by end of September, FERC will impose its own reforms on PJM.

fr-conference-date.speaker: FERC, Notice of Commission-Led Technical Conference (Docket AD26-7-000)
fr-conference-date.evidence: The technical conference will convene on Thursday, July 23, 2026, in the Kevin J. McIntyre Commission Meeting Room at the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, 888 First Street NE, Washington, DC 20426. The conference will discuss PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.'s (PJM) governance and stakeholder process, with a particular focus on identifying and evaluating actionable reforms to improve PJM's ability to address system needs in a timely and efficient manner.

isone-abeyance.speaker: ISO New England (ISO Newswire)
isone-abeyance.evidence: ISO New England and the region's transmission owners intend to request a 90-day abeyance as part of compliance with a show cause order issued by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC). The ISO and transmission owners must submit interconnection process modifications by November 16, 2026, following the abeyance period if approved. By July 20, the ISO must file with FERC an informational report on resource adequacy in the context of large loads.

isone-report.speaker: ISO New England (ISO Newswire)
isone-report.evidence: ISO-NE has made an informational filing on regional resource adequacy and has begun to outline potential rule changes, including requiring new large loads to bring incremental new generation, and not procuring capacity through the regional capacity market to serve these large loads. During a July 16 presentation to the NEPOOL Transmission Committee, ISO-NE outlined plans to request a 90-day abeyance of the show cause proceeding.

pjm-bra.speaker: PJM Interconnection news release
pjm-bra.evidence: PJM's 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction procured 138,318 MW of unforced capacity. The price came in at the FERC-approved cap of $325/MW-day (UCAP) for the entire PJM footprint. The cleared supply procured in the auction times the clearing price totals $16.4 billion. The capacity of the resources procured in the auction, plus FRR resources, is short of PJM's 20% installed reserve margin target by 6,831 MW. PJM continues to hold a reserve margin of 14.7% for the 2028/2029 Delivery Year.

lacerte-wires.speaker: David LaCerte, FERC Commissioner
lacerte-wires.evidence: status quo is really untenable. Looking at things differently is hard, especially in entrenched utilities that have been doing this for a long time. We have a lot of other models at other RTOs and ISOs across the country that are much more functional. We need to make sure that the incentives that we give are properly tailored to actually meet the goals.
lacerte-wires.note: Utility Dive renders the first phrase as a partial quote inside its own sentence ('The PJM Interconnection's "status quo is really untenable"'), so only the words inside the inner quotation marks are his; the site quotes that fragment and no more.

md-delegation-letter.speaker: Maryland Congressional Delegation (Sens. Van Hollen and Alsobrooks; Reps. Hoyer, Mfume, Raskin, Ivey, Elfreth, McClain Delaney and Olszewski)
md-delegation-letter.occasion: Letter to FERC Chairman Swett, July 27, 2026
md-delegation-letter.evidence: We were encouraged by the Commission's June 18, 2026 orders directing PJM and five other grid operators to justify or reform how they assign the costs of serving large loads, which advance the essential goal of protecting ordinary consumers. We urge the Commission to act expeditiously to provide relief from these costs for Maryland ratepayers, including as requested in OPC's complaint.
md-delegation-letter.note: Read directly from the signed PDF with fitz, not from a summary. The letter cites $22 billion in PJM projects advanced principally to serve data centers, roughly $2 billion of it assigned to Maryland ratepayers, and an estimated $1.6 billion on Maryland bills over ten years, $823 million of it residential, about $345 for the average customer. It asks for relief as requested in the Maryland OPC complaint at Docket EL26-63, not for retroactive refunds.

spanberger-scc.speaker: Abigail Spanberger, Governor of Virginia
spanberger-scc.occasion: Statement on the Virginia SCC order, August 10, 2026
spanberger-scc.evidence: I am proud that after my administration urged state regulators to protect Virginia families and small businesses from shouldering the cost of new transmission infrastructure meant to serve data centers, the SCC listened. This order \u2014 which is projected to save Virginians hundreds of millions of dollars \u2014 makes sure that data centers are paying the full cost of the transmission infrastructure their developments require.
spanberger-scc.note: The release does not mention FERC or PJM; it is state retail action running parallel to the federal proceeding.

sherrill-fairshare.speaker: Mikie Sherrill, Governor of New Jersey
sherrill-fairshare.occasion: Signing of the Data Center Fair Share Act (S731/A796), July 7, 2026
sherrill-fairshare.evidence: For too long, New Jersey families have paid the price for poor oversight, outdated policies, and rising demand on our electric grid by unchecked actors.
sherrill-fairshare.note: The bill creates a data-center ratepayer class, requires large loads to curtail before residential customers on a strained grid, and lets large loads offset capacity obligations by funding demand reduction elsewhere.

opsi-forcefully-oppose.evidence: Should the Members nonetheless approve their term sheet, the states will forcefully oppose it before the Commission and beyond.
